findings.description: Dissent findings using the supplied schema have symbol anchors such as `src/module.py:function` and numeric `anchor_line` fields. This reader forwards the symbol anchor but ignores `anchor_line`, while its fallback requires separate file/path fields.
findings.failure_mode: The citation parser cannot extract a numeric citation from these findings, so valid dissent detections disappear from gates-combined.md and receive no recall credit.
findings.suggested_fix: For symbol anchors, extract the file component and combine it with anchor_line and optional anchor_line_end. Preserve support for existing numeric citations.

findings.description: all_pass ignores the command's recorded exit status and timeout flag whenever its output contains a parseable passing summary.
findings.failure_mode: A TAP command that prints its plan and passing results before failing or hanging during cleanup is accepted as fully passing. An APPROVED gate can consequently receive verdict_accuracy=true even though its test command failed or timed out.
findings.suggested_fix: Require rc == 0 and timed_out == false in all_pass. Propagate command failures into grading summaries and self-check decisions even when individual test results were parsed.

findings.description: ABS_WORD treats any quoted token beginning with '/' as a path candidate, and the only regex exemption is a single-component '/x/'. Legitimate Bash tool calls therefore produce an `outside_path` contamination verdict: `sed -n '/start/,/end/p'` yields the word `/start/,/end/p` (',' and '/' are in the word class) which is not '^/[^/]+/$' and is outside every allowed root; `grep -rn '"/api/users"' src/` yields `/api/users`; `python3 -c 're.sub(r"/x", ...)'` yields `/x`. Loa tasks are bash/sed heavy, so this fires on ordinary agent commands in the IMPLEMENT phase. Because contamination is the field that decides whether a run is admissible for the ablation analysis, a false hit silently discards valid runs and biases arm comparisons; the header's 'lower bound' caveat covers misses, not false positives.
findings.failure_mode: grade.json records contaminated={pattern: outside_path} for runs whose agent only used sed address ranges or quoted route/regex strings; those runs are excluded or flagged, corrupting the ablation result set.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat a Bash word as a path when it resolves to something path-like: require that the first component after '/' matches an allowed-root prefix or an existing-directory name, skip words that contain ',' or appear inside quotes following sed/awk/grep/python -c, and drop any word containing regex metacharacters (`^ $ * + ? [ ] ( ) | \`). Alternatively restrict `outside_path` to the explicit path fields (Read/Write/Edit/Glob) and for Bash only check words that follow known file-taking commands (cat, less, head, tail, cp, mv, ls, cd, source, .).

findings.description: remove_path walks a directory with os.walk (followlinks=False) and calls os.chmod(..., 0o700) on every entry in `ds`. os.walk places symlinks-to-directories in `ds`, and os.chmod follows symlinks by default, so the chmod lands on the link target. remove_path runs on agent-controlled content: put_file calls it on an existing `dst` inside the final/snapshot tree (the agent may have made the hidden test's dest a directory containing `x -> /home/<grader-user>` or `-> <suite-root>/tasks/...`). The grader always runs on the host regardless of --executor, so this changes modes on host directories outside the grading tree.
findings.failure_mode: An agent-created directory at a hidden dest containing a symlink to a writable host directory gets that directory chmod'ed to 0o700 by the grader (e.g. the user's project checkout or the suite fixture directory loses group/other permissions); shutil.rmtree is symlink-safe but the pre-pass is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip symlinks in the chmod pre-pass: `if not os.path.islink(full): os.chmod(full, 0o700)` (or use `os.chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False)` guarded by `os.chmod in os.supports_follow_symlinks`). Also apply the same pre-pass only to directories created by the grader, not to agent-provided subtrees.

findings.description: extract_snapshot returns False without any diagnostic when the bundle file is missing, index.json has no/invalid commit, `git init`, `git bundle unbundle` (e.g. a thin bundle with unmet prerequisites) or `git archive` fails. In grade() a False result just `continue`s, so verdict_accuracy_per_gate stays null and snapshots_graded omits the label. A run where REVIEW produced a trailer but the snapshot could not be read is therefore indistinguishable in grade.json from one that was never attempted, and nothing is printed to stderr. Across a batch this silently drops verdict-accuracy coverage with no signal to the operator.
findings.failure_mode: A pipeline-run.sh bundle-format change or a corrupt IMPLEMENT.bundle makes every verdict_accuracy null for the batch; ablation-row.sh aggregates nulls as 'gate did not run' and no one notices.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a stderr warning naming the label and the failing step, and record the reason in grade.json (e.g. `snapshot_errors: {implement: "unbundle failed"}`) so a missing accuracy is attributable. Consider making a present-but-unreadable bundle a GradeError (exit 2) when the corresponding gate ran.

findings.description: The final tree is 'sandbox/ as the agent left it' and only paths listed in grader_protected are restored from the fixture. pytest is invoked with `--rootdir /workspace`, so an agent-added root `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options]`, `setup.cfg` or `tox.ini` is still loaded (python -I only drops cwd/user-site from sys.path; pytest inserts rootdir itself for conftest import). A conftest hook or an `addopts`/`python_files` setting changes how the hidden tests are collected and reported, and the seeders only add grader_protected entries for infrastructure files that already exist in the fixture, so a root file the fixture lacks is never neutralised. The static_cases floor stops total from shrinking but does not stop hidden tests from being reported as passing. This is the ablation's primary metric, so the result can be moved by a routine agent action (adding a conftest with fixtures) without any intent to game.
findings.failure_mode: hidden_tests.passed/total and snapshot-based verdict_accuracy reflect agent-controlled pytest configuration rather than the hidden tests' real outcome; arms differ by how often agents add root config files.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the pytest/bats configuration surface as implicitly grader_protected: for build tasks always restore-or-remove root `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, and every `conftest.py` on the path from rootdir to each hidden test dest (restored from the fixture when present, deleted otherwise). Alternatively pass `-c <grader-owned ini>` plus `--noconftest` and ship required fixtures via hidden/manifest.json.

findings.description: all_pass requires passed >= total, and total is max(pytest total, static_cases) where pytest total includes `skipped`/`xfailed` and static_cases counts every `def test…(` in the hidden files regardless of whether pytest collects it (nested helper defs, methods on non-Test classes, functions excluded by a marker). Any hidden test that is skipped on the grading image (platform/skipif) or any uncollected `test_` helper makes all_pass permanently False for every tree. Consequences: `--self-check reference` can never PASS for that task (reference run has passed < total), suite_green_* is always False for refactor tasks, and every APPROVED gate verdict is scored inaccurate.
findings.failure_mode: A hidden test file with one `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform…)` or a `def test_helper()` nested in a test yields self-check reference FAIL and verdict_accuracy false on every run of that task, with no indication that the grader rather than the agent is at fault.
findings.suggested_fix: Define all_pass on outcomes rather than counts: `not res['bad'] and not res['parse_error'] and res['passed'] + skipped + xfailed >= total`, and compute static_cases only from top-level/`class Test*` defs (or drop the static floor to `max(total, len(order))` when the summary parsed). Have `--self-check reference` print the per-test ids that block PASS so authors can see a skipped/uncollected case.

findings.description: In container mode the outer subprocess.run(timeout=TEST_TIMEOUT_S + 60) kills only the `docker run` client process when it fires (e.g. the in-container `timeout 120` was defeated by a process ignoring SIGTERM, or the daemon is slow). The container itself keeps running; `--rm` removes it only after it exits on its own. The grader then proceeds, treating the run as timed_out, while a detached container still holds the bind mount on `<run-dir>/grading/final` and CPU.
findings.failure_mode: A hidden test that hangs in a SIGTERM-ignoring subprocess leaves one orphaned container per graded run; a batch grade accumulates stuck containers holding mounts on grading trees that the next grade call tries to delete via fresh_dir (EBUSY/partial removal).
findings.suggested_fix: Give each container a unique `--name` and on TimeoutExpired run `docker kill <name>` (and `docker rm -f`) before returning; or add `--init` and `--stop-timeout` and use `timeout -k 5 120` inside so the in-container kill is reliable.

findings.cross_file_justification: seed-refactor-tasks.sh writes refactor tasks whose test_command is the fixture's covering tests (e.g. `python3 -m pytest -q tests/unit`) and instructs the author to add the hand-written structural check to hidden/manifest.json; ablation-grade.sh then runs test_command on the base tree after overlaying that structural check.
findings.description: For refactor tasks, suite_green_base is computed by running test_command on the base tree AFTER prepare() has overlaid every hidden/manifest.json entry, including the structural check file. If the structural check's dest lies inside a directory the covering test_command collects (the natural place, beside the covered tests), it is red at base by design, so suite_green_base is False for every graded run and `--self-check base` (which requires 'structural red and suite green') can never PASS. Nothing in the seeder output or validate-suite.sh warns about this coupling; static_cases excludes the structural file but the run does not.
findings.failure_mode: Every refactor task whose structural check lives under the covered test directory reports suite_green_base=false and fails its base self-check, so authors either cannot freeze the task or ship it with a permanently false baseline that masks real regressions.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude the structural check when measuring the suite: run test_command on a base/final tree without the structural overlay (or pass `--deselect`/`--ignore=<structural dest>` for pytest and omit the file for bats), or require in load_task that the structural check's dest is not under any path argument of test_command and emit a clear GradeError otherwise.
